15 — AI Evaluation and Regression Checklist#

Verify that AI-enabled applications have representative, measurable, repeatable evaluation of task quality and safety, and that changes are held to defined regression and release standards. Scores from a benchmark, a model judge, or a dashboard alone do not prove real-world correctness or absence of harm.

Scope: AI-specific. This file is one part of the 15_AI_Evaluation_and_Regression.md checklist. Apply the domain-wide release gate across all applicable scope files; each checklist ID remains unique.

Review details#

  • Project / product:
  • Release / version / environment:
  • Scope and applicable jurisdictions / markets:
  • Evaluated tasks, models, agents, retrieval, and user populations:
  • Golden dataset / evaluator / model and prompt versions:
  • Task, safety, latency, cost, and regression thresholds:
  • Evaluator / domain / risk approvers:
  • Review date:
  • Decision: Pending / Approved / Approved with documented exceptions / Blocked

How to use#

  1. Copy this shared checklist into project-specific evaluation records. Leave the repository's reusable checkbox items unchecked.
  2. Define task outcomes, severe failures, baseline performance, and release thresholds before inspecting candidate results. Use separate measures for task success, policy/safety, retrieval, downstream tool actions, user experience, and operational cost where applicable.
  3. Mark [x] only when verified from versioned dataset manifests, reproducible runs, validated scorers, qualified human reviews, CI outcomes, or a documented approver decision. Keep evidence, failures, exceptions, and genuine N/A reasons outside this template, indexed by EVAL ID.
  4. Compare under equivalent settings; account for stochastic generation, sample size, evaluator bias, and real-world coverage limitations. A high aggregate score must never hide a severe individual failure.
  5. Apply ## API Checks and ## Frontend Checks independently for supported interfaces. Document inapplicable items in project review records.
  6. Re-run appropriate evaluations after model, prompt, retrieval, dataset, guardrail, API, tool, or frontend changes. Coordinate model selection, data curation, governance, safety/red teaming, and monitoring in their separate checklists.

Task metrics and success criteria#

  • EVAL-001 Define each AI-enabled user task, its intended outcome, and which system components the evaluation covers.
  • EVAL-002 Distinguish model-only capability evaluation from full product workflow and user-outcome evaluation.
  • EVAL-003 Assign a named business owner, evaluation owner, and qualified risk reviewer for each release-critical task.
  • EVAL-004 Choose task-specific primary quality metrics and document the units, calculation, direction, and acceptance threshold.
  • EVAL-005 Define separate severe-failure categories such as unauthorized actions, data disclosure, misleading high-impact advice, and materially incorrect decisions.
  • EVAL-006 Select safety, privacy, reliability, latency, accessibility, and cost guardrails appropriate to the deployment risk.
  • EVAL-007 Define whether precision, recall, F1, exact match, task completion, calibration, or human preference appropriately reflects success.
  • EVAL-008 Distinguish false positives from false negatives and agree which error types have greater real-world impact.
  • EVAL-009 Define correct abstention, refusal, request-for-clarification, and human-escalation behavior as measurable outcomes.
  • EVAL-010 Set acceptable rates for unsupported factual claims and incorrect citations where evidence-grounded answers are promised.
  • EVAL-011 Measure retrieval relevance separately from answer groundedness and completeness when the workflow uses RAG.
  • EVAL-012 Evaluate tool selection, argument correctness, permissions, side effects, and handoff completion when agents are used.
  • EVAL-013 Specify output-schema validity, required fields, parser errors, and downstream contract success where structured responses are required.
  • EVAL-014 Include multilingual, multimodal, long-context, and relevant subgroup metrics when supported by the product and allowed by applicable rules.
  • EVAL-015 Record target user cohorts, task difficulty, acceptable task duration, and normal versus adverse operating conditions.
  • EVAL-016 Agree baseline and candidate comparison rules before looking at the evaluation results.
  • EVAL-017 Define appropriate sample sizes, uncertainty reporting, and acceptable statistical or practical change in each critical metric.
  • EVAL-018 Document the expected cost per successful task and latency under representative concurrency rather than only per-model token prices.
  • EVAL-019 Specify which metrics must not regress even if the aggregate task-quality score improves.
  • EVAL-020 Document known unmeasurable harms, evaluation blind spots, and required compensating review for consequential use cases.
  • EVAL-021 Require relevant stakeholders to sign off on evaluation definitions before promoting a new model, prompt, or workflow.
  • EVAL-022 Review metric relevance when product goals, user populations, model authority, or supported modalities change.

Golden datasets and representative cases#

  • EVAL-023 Maintain a versioned golden or reference dataset whose records have stable IDs, expected outcomes, and task-specific metadata.
  • EVAL-024 Document source, consent or licensing restrictions, sampling method, review owner, and permissible use for each evaluation dataset.
  • EVAL-025 Sample representative authorized production task patterns or well-founded synthetic cases without including prohibited personal data.
  • EVAL-026 Keep a frozen holdout set separate from examples used to tune prompts, select models, or train evaluators.
  • EVAL-027 Audit train, tuning, evaluation, and holdout overlap including duplicate, near-duplicate, translated, and augmented examples.
  • EVAL-028 Include ordinary, edge, ambiguous, adverse, and high-consequence cases based on real expected use.
  • EVAL-029 Use realistic multi-turn conversations and full workflow state for tasks that depend on conversational history.
  • EVAL-030 Include negative cases requiring safe refusals, abstention, missing-context handling, or clarification.
  • EVAL-031 Add adversarial prompt injection and untrusted retrieved-content cases with safe test accounts and simulated tool effects.
  • EVAL-032 Include malformed, long, truncated, encoded, multilingual, and mixed-modality inputs relevant to supported interfaces.
  • EVAL-033 Represent major customer cohorts, feature flags, locales, supported channels, and risk-relevant conditions where permissible.
  • EVAL-034 Test time-sensitive facts, outdated knowledge, conflicting evidence, and stale or missing retrieved documents where applicable.
  • EVAL-035 Include scenarios with third-party API errors, retrieval failures, tool timeouts, partial work, and safe retries.
  • EVAL-036 Record expected outcomes as objective assertions, acceptable alternative answers, rubric grades, or authorized reference judgments.
  • EVAL-037 Use expert adjudication where valid answers vary or ground truth is genuinely uncertain rather than inventing one exact answer.
  • EVAL-038 Check that labels and expected answers remain aligned with current product policies, authoritative sources, and versioned schemas.
  • EVAL-039 Mark examples that became obsolete due to product changes and retain a review history before updating expectations.
  • EVAL-040 Track dataset size, coverage gaps, class balance, source freshness, and severe-case counts at every released version.
  • EVAL-041 Protect sensitive golden cases from unauthorized access, public embedding, and external model-evaluator transmission.
  • EVAL-042 Create an approved process for adding sanitized production incidents and user feedback to the regression collection.
  • EVAL-043 Require test records to reference versioned tool responses, search results, model inputs, and environment fixtures where needed for replay.
  • EVAL-044 Verify dataset parsing, evaluation prompt rendering, and expected-answer mapping on hand-checked fixtures.
  • EVAL-045 Ensure test labels, scoring rationales, and sample metadata cannot leak into the model input unless the task requires them.
  • EVAL-046 Freeze a released dataset manifest and checksum or equivalent immutable reference for reproducible comparisons.

Human and automated evaluation#

  • EVAL-047 Use deterministic assertions for machine-verifiable outputs such as schema validity, field values, authorized tool calls, and required refusals.
  • EVAL-048 Choose task-specific algorithmic metrics only when their assumptions match the expected output and user need.
  • EVAL-049 Define human grading rubrics with observable criteria, anchors, positive/negative examples, and explicit scoring instructions.
  • EVAL-050 Recruit qualified reviewers with domain, language, and cultural knowledge appropriate to sensitive and consequential tasks.
  • EVAL-051 Calibrate human reviewers on a representative set of examples before collecting release-critical judgments.
  • EVAL-052 Measure inter-rater agreement or disagreement using methods appropriate to the rating scale and task.
  • EVAL-053 Use independent adjudication for disputed high-impact labels or reviews rather than averaging away genuine differences.
  • EVAL-054 Randomize answer order and blind candidate identities where feasible to reduce preference and position bias.
  • EVAL-055 Check human reviewers are not shown sensitive information beyond their authorized role and approved purpose.
  • EVAL-056 Assess annotator burden and exposure to potentially distressing content; provide appropriate support and escalation.
  • EVAL-057 Validate model-based graders against expert human labels and known good/bad examples before trusting their verdicts.
  • EVAL-058 Check model-judge position, verbosity, language, self-preference, and reference-answer leakage biases where relevant.
  • EVAL-059 Version automated grading prompts, judge model snapshots, thresholds, and any external evaluation services.
  • EVAL-060 Test scorer behavior for empty outputs, formatting errors, timeouts, parse failures, and partial evaluation jobs.
  • EVAL-061 Distinguish a failed system response from a failed judge or unavailable evaluation service in reporting.
  • EVAL-062 Use paired candidate comparisons where practical and keep model settings and test fixtures comparable.
  • EVAL-063 Repeat stochastic model evaluations enough to characterize variance for release-critical decisions.
  • EVAL-064 Record confidence intervals or suitable uncertainty estimates and avoid claiming significance from small score differences.
  • EVAL-065 Report per-case and per-subgroup results along with aggregate scores so serious failures are not hidden.
  • EVAL-066 Separate retrieval ranking quality, groundedness, citation validity, and answer completeness in RAG evaluations.
  • EVAL-067 Grade agent task success using confirmed tool states and correct authorization, not merely persuasive model narratives.
  • EVAL-068 Evaluate user-visible task success, comprehension, safe behavior, and recovery through targeted usability testing where suitable.
  • EVAL-069 Compare automatic grades and real-user complaints to detect metric gaming or poor agreement with human utility.
  • EVAL-070 Control evaluation compute budget, data retention, external judge permissions, and reproducibility settings.
  • EVAL-071 Store failures and reviewer rationales securely for investigation without retaining unnecessary private full transcripts.
  • EVAL-072 Require an explicit evaluator-quality review before changing the scoring approach that blocks or approves releases.

Regression and release thresholds#

  • EVAL-073 Establish an approved production baseline for each critical evaluation suite, including exact model, prompt, data, tool, and evaluator versions.
  • EVAL-074 Trigger relevant evaluation suites for changes to model snapshots, prompts, retrieval, fine-tuning, tool definitions, policy, or output parsers.
  • EVAL-075 Define smoke, targeted, full regression, and adversarial suites with risk-based execution times and ownership.
  • EVAL-076 Run relevant quality and safety gates in CI or equivalent controlled release workflows, not only manually after launch.
  • EVAL-077 Preserve run identifiers, timestamps, source revisions, dataset manifests, judge versions, environment, and inference settings.
  • EVAL-078 Compare candidate and baseline results using identical cases and fair configurations wherever possible.
  • EVAL-079 Set predeclared absolute performance floors and maximum allowed regression deltas for each launch-critical metric.
  • EVAL-080 Make severe safety, unauthorized-action, or privacy violations individually blocking when required rather than averaging them into a quality score.
  • EVAL-081 Account for stochastic variability, repeated runs, and confidence limits when deciding whether a small observed delta is meaningful.
  • EVAL-082 Detect flaky tests and isolate environmental or evaluator failures without silently ignoring real application regressions.
  • EVAL-083 Require owner review of newly failing cases, newly passing cases, and cases whose scores moved materially.
  • EVAL-084 Prevent test-set edits or metric-weight changes from being used to conceal a known regression without review.
  • EVAL-085 Define a documented waiver process with rationale, severity, accountable approver, expiration, and retest plan.
  • EVAL-086 Check that low-frequency but high-consequence tests stay visible in release reports even when their sample size is small.
  • EVAL-087 Validate API schema, error handling, permissions, and downstream integration behavior alongside model-level metrics.
  • EVAL-088 Test representative production load, latency, token usage, context size, throughput, and per-task cost for changed configurations.
  • EVAL-089 Use shadow, canary, feature flags, or limited rollout when offline tests cannot capture important real-world outcomes.
  • EVAL-090 Define production guardrails and stop conditions for unexpected refusal changes, user complaints, harmful outputs, or task failures.
  • EVAL-091 Ensure rollback or fallback configurations have been tested against compatible prompts, schemas, and permitted tool capabilities.
  • EVAL-092 Correlate production quality indicators and incident reports with the exact deployed evaluation baseline and model/configuration revisions.
  • EVAL-093 Collect privacy-preserving production feedback and representative user reports as candidates for future regression fixtures.
  • EVAL-094 Review whether data or concept drift makes the held-out evaluation set less representative of current traffic.
  • EVAL-095 Reevaluate evaluation metrics and samples when business policy, user population, or downstream consequences change.
  • EVAL-096 Record a final go/no-go decision and remaining accepted risks against the exact candidate release.

Frontend Checks#

Apply these client-side checks only when the AI feature has a user-facing or reviewer-facing interface. They remain part of this AI domain; the general frontend checklist inventory is separate.

  • EVAL-117 Evaluate complete user journeys and representative device/browser conditions in addition to isolated model text outputs.
  • EVAL-118 Show appropriate uncertainty, no-answer, refusal, or escalation UI for cases where the model cannot meet the task.
  • EVAL-119 Verify citations and factual evidence displayed in the UI support the corresponding claims when source-grounding is promised.
  • EVAL-120 Test how users perceive model-generated suggestions compared with independently verified facts or committed external actions.
  • EVAL-121 Check output rendering for malformed markup, long text, unsupported characters, streaming, tables, and structured widgets.
  • EVAL-122 Ensure user-visible failures, timeouts, missing context, and rejected tool actions have accessible recovery paths.
  • EVAL-123 Test keyboard, assistive-technology, and focus behavior for AI-generated dynamic content and error states.
  • EVAL-124 Validate that localization, multilingual input, and supported multimodal flows are represented in regression tests.
  • EVAL-125 Compare page/task latency, time-to-first-content, and completion time before and after model or prompt changes.
  • EVAL-126 Test how frontend caches, old browser tabs, or feature flags behave with new prompt and response formats.
  • EVAL-127 Confirm client-side validation and rendering cannot make an unsafe model response executable.
  • EVAL-128 Verify agent actions appear as proposed, pending, approved, or confirmed only when supported by authoritative state.
  • EVAL-129 Include approved user research and comprehension checks where automation bias or overreliance is a material risk.
  • EVAL-130 Ensure test interfaces do not display restricted golden answers, private evaluation prompts, or secret reference data to unauthorized users.
  • EVAL-131 Make feedback and report-an-error controls usable for incorrect, harmful, or inaccessible AI output.
  • EVAL-132 Check that production feedback tagging records the deployed model/configuration without collecting unnecessary personal data.
  • EVAL-133 Evaluate user experience of staged rollout and fallback when a different model changes output length, tone, or available features.
  • EVAL-134 Test visible safety warnings and confirmations for high-impact workflows before release.
  • EVAL-135 Review mobile and low-bandwidth behavior under slow or failing evaluation-relevant AI services.
  • EVAL-136 Check important frontend regressions and support escalations against release-approved user-task metrics.

Release gate#

  • The exact release has approved task definitions, meaningful primary metrics, severe-failure conditions, risk guardrails, and predeclared acceptance thresholds.
  • Golden and held-out evaluation cases are representative of the intended deployment, versioned, permissioned, contamination-checked, and reviewed for major coverage gaps.
  • Deterministic assertions and model-based graders are fit for purpose; human rubrics and automated judge scores have suitable calibration and auditability.
  • Candidate and approved baseline results are compared with reproducible settings, adequate repeatability, and explicit statistical or practical uncertainty where needed.
  • All release-blocking privacy, safety, authorization, and consequential task failures are resolved or have the specifically required authorized disposition; averaging does not waive critical failures.
  • API, retrieval, agent/tool, and frontend end-to-end paths meet the relevant quality, contract, usability, accessibility, latency, and cost requirements.
  • CI/controlled release gates, anomaly and regression review, safe rollback, production observation, and accountable incident response are ready.
  • A named release approver has reviewed run artifacts, per-case regressions, coverage limitations, accepted risks, and the precise model/data/prompt/guardrail versions promoted.

Domain-specific approval rule: Block sign-off when the evaluation suite is materially unrepresentative or contaminated, scoring is unvalidated for decisions it controls, a severe user-impacting or unauthorized-action failure is unresolved, or an important metric regresses beyond its approved threshold without qualified acceptance. Passing these checks is not proof of complete AI safety, impartiality, or compliance with any particular jurisdiction.

Trusted references and scope#

The following official frameworks, provider documentation, and tool-maintainer references informed these project-specific verification questions. They are not universal requirements or substitutes for independent evaluation design.

  • NIST AI RMF Playbook — Measure — risk-based evaluation methods, uncertainty, deployment conditions, and measurement gaps.
  • NIST AI RMF Generative AI Profile (AI 600-1) — generative AI risk identification, evaluation, and trustworthiness considerations.
  • OpenAI API — Evaluation best practices — task-specific evals, representative cases, model variability, calibration, and development-driven regression.
  • OpenAI API — Graders — deterministic and model-based grading, human reference scores, grader limitations; note platform deprecation.
  • Microsoft Foundry — Evaluation overview — evaluation workflow, datasets, response generation, quality/safety metrics, and production traces.
  • Microsoft Foundry — Built-in Evaluators — task completion, retrieval, groundedness, safety, and textual similarity metrics.
  • Microsoft Foundry — RAG Evaluators — separate retrieval-process and grounded-answer system evaluation.
  • Google Cloud — Gen AI evaluation service overview — adaptive task rubrics, version/model comparisons, production sampling, and synthetic test cases.
  • Amazon Bedrock — Automatic model evaluation jobs — task-specific dataset jobs, settings, built-in metrics, and evaluation artifacts.
  • Amazon Bedrock — Human model evaluation jobs — human review teams, task-specific instructions, qualitative comparisons, and grading controls.
  • Amazon Bedrock — LLM-as-a-judge evaluation jobs — judge-model evaluation configuration, IAM, datasets, and permissions.
  • Ragas — Available evaluation metrics — RAG faithfulness/retrieval and agent task/tool metrics where this library is chosen.

Applicability: NIST AI RMF and its GenAI profile are voluntary risk frameworks, not certifications. As of November 2026, the OpenAI Evals platform and associated graders are being retired (read-only after October 31; scheduled closure November 30); avoid building new long-lived release gates dependent on that service and verify the latest migration guidance. Microsoft, Google, and AWS evaluation features, model judges, and scoring thresholds are platform-specific and may have version, regional, or preview limitations. Ragas metrics are implementation choices, not a universal scientific gold standard. Protect evaluation data and check legal rights before sharing it with third-party judges.

Source review date: 2026-11-12.

Suggested testing tools#

Choose tools appropriate to the project's stack and risks; automation supports evidence but does not approve the checklist.

  • Test focus: held-out cases, severe failures, judge calibration, and CI quality thresholds; include model and dataset behaviors where applicable.
  • Cross-stack: promptfoo.
  • Python: DeepEval + Ragas + pytest; for pytest-based suites, run python -m pytest -q.
  • TypeScript: promptfoo + Vitest; for Vitest-based suites, run npx vitest run (or npx playwright test for E2E).
  • JavaScript: promptfoo + Jest; for Jest-based suites, run npx jest --ci (or npx playwright test for E2E).
  • Evidence: Save tool versions, configuration, test environment, fixtures, results, and links in project-specific review records using the existing checklist IDs. Expert review remains necessary where relevant.

Suggested AI skills for verification#

These are optional agent review aids, not automated passes or release approval. Each linked repository had at least 1,000 GitHub stars when checked on 2026-11-12; counts are per repository, not per skill, and do not indicate security or correctness.

  • agentic-eval — Check end-to-end agent outcome regressions (github/awesome-copilot, 41,073 repo stars).
  • eval-driven-dev — Test evaluation-based development gates (github/awesome-copilot, 41,073 repo stars).
  • llm-evaluation — Review datasets, graders, and quality thresholds (wshobson/agents, 42,437 repo stars).

How to check: In a project-specific copy, have the agent audit the AI-specific scope and map findings to this file's existing checklist IDs, with code/configuration references, reproducible test results, failed or inapplicable cases, and uncertainties. Independently verify findings; keep shared template boxes unchecked and retain human approval requirements.

Before use: Read the skill's SKILL.md, referenced scripts, license, and requested tool permissions. Only execute vetted skills with appropriate access in a controlled environment.

Important warning: reference only#

⚠️ Reference only — not a definitive or exhaustive checklist. This template is a starting point for review, not the ultimate authority or a guarantee of project safety, quality, regulatory compliance, accessibility, security, or launch readiness.

Use project-specific judgment and independent verification. Requirements and risks evolve and differ by project, technology, and jurisdiction. Adapt the checks, consult current authoritative sources, perform relevant tests, and obtain qualified specialist review or approval when appropriate. Checking every box does not replace these steps.

Reference, not a certification. Check applicability, verify important claims against current primary sources, and seek expert review where necessary. Suggest an improvement.
